## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

Each run was sampled at harvest, and the harvest sample was assayed for the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` modelled responses. The clarified harvest was assayed for host cell protein and residual DNA in the studies that @sec-chronology lists. Across the `{python} N_HD` runs assayed, host cell protein in the clarified harvest ranged from `{python} s3(HCP_MIN)` to `{python} s3(HCP_MAX)` ng/mg and DNA from `{python} s3(DNA_MIN)` to `{python} s3(DNA_MAX)` pg/mg. The step carries no criterion for either. The culture was monitored through each run for viable cell density, viability and the principal metabolites under SOP-2003, and these records are not in the study record (PD-003-09).

Each run carries the number it has in the standard order of its design, the "Run" column of the design tables in Appendices A and B, and this report cites runs by that number. The runs were made in randomized order. The `{python} words(NC_SCR)` centre points of the screening design were made at positions `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in CP_ORDER['screening']])` of its `{python} N_SCR` runs, and the `{python} words(NC_RSM)` centre points of the response-surface design at positions `{python} join_and([str(x) for x in CP_ORDER['rsm']])` of its `{python} N_PLAN` runs. Of the augmentation runs, `{python} words(len(AUG_REP))` repeat a setting of the planned design (runs `{python} AUG_REP_A` repeat runs `{python} AUG_REP_P`). They lie in the other block, so the analysis does not count them as pure error, and the pure error of the models fitted to all runs comes from the centre points of the response-surface design.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

The designs were generated, randomized and analysed under SOP-1002, with the methods of PCMP-001 §6 [@montgomery2017]. Each factor was coded so that its set-point is 0 and the ends of its range studied are −1 and +1. For this step the set-point of every factor of the designs lies at the centre of its range studied, so the centre points of the designs are at the set-points.

The screening data were fitted by least squares to the `{python} words(len(SFS))` main effects and the `{python} words(N_2FI_S)` two-factor interactions. An effect is twice the coded coefficient, the change in the response across the full range studied. The model has `{python} N_SCR_TERMS` terms with the intercept in `{python} N_SCR` runs. It leaves `{python} words(SDF_LOF)` degree of freedom for lack of fit and `{python} words(SDF_PE)` for pure error. With so few, R² overstates how well the model would predict new runs, so the screening analysis was read only to identify active factors and interactions. Its lack-of-fit test compares the mean of the centre points with the mean of the factorial runs, which is the test for curvature.

PCP-003 prescribes the full quadratic model of each response-surface output, with `{python} N_FULL` terms besides the intercept. The outputs were analysed instead by the model selection that INV-002 adopted on `{python} CA3_DATE` as its corrective action CA3, recorded as the discrepancy PD-003-03. It has three steps.

1. The scale. The Box-Cox profile of the full quadratic model gives the exponent λ that best makes the residuals normal with constant variance, with its 95 % interval [@boxcox1964]. An output is modelled on the log scale where that interval contains 0, the log, and excludes 1, the raw scale. It is modelled on the raw scale otherwise.
2. The model. Among all `{python} f"{NCAND:,}"` submodels of the full quadratic that keep hierarchy, the model with the lowest AICc is taken. A submodel keeps hierarchy when it contains an interaction only with both its main effects, and a square only with its main effect.
3. The check. The selected model is judged against the adequacy criteria of PCP-003 §7, listed below.

AICc estimates how well a model would predict new runs. It rewards a smaller residual and penalises every estimated term, and its small-sample correction raises the penalty when the runs are few for the number of terms, as in these designs [@hurvich1989; @burnham2002]. A stepwise search changes one term at a time and stops when no single change lowers AICc, so it can stop where only a combination of changes would lower it further. On the data of this step a forward search would have stopped at a model with a higher AICc for acidic variants, and a backward search for aggregate.

The models were fitted to all `{python} N_ALL` runs, the `{python} N_PLAN` planned runs and the `{python} N_AUG` augmentation runs, with a block term coded −1 for the planned runs and +1 for the augmentation. A prediction is made with the block term at 0, the average of the two blocks.

Of the modelled attributes, `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in LOGR])` are modelled on the log scale. On that scale the model reads ln(y) = b0 + b1·x1 + … + e. Transformed back, y = e^b0^ · e^b1·x1^ · … · e^e^, so a main effect multiplies the output by e^2b^ from the low to the high end of its range when the other factors are at their set-points, where the interaction terms vanish. The error between runs multiplies the output too, so its size in percentage points grows with the level of the output. For high mannose and acidic variants this is expected, because the precision of the glycan map and of icIEF is a percentage of the level (Appendix D). For aggregate the profile supports the log scale too, although the precision of SEC is an absolute amount. Least squares, and the tests and prediction intervals built on it, assume residuals that are independent and normally distributed with mean zero and the same variance over the whole range studied. On the raw scale, the residual standard deviation of these outputs in the upper half of the predicted values is `{python} f"{min(RAWSPR[r][0] for r in LOGR):.2f}"` to `{python} f"{max(RAWSPR[r][0] for r in LOGR):.2f}"` times that in the lower half. On the log scale the ratio is `{python} f"{min(RAWSPR[r][1] for r in LOGR):.2f}"` to `{python} f"{max(RAWSPR[r][1] for r in LOGR):.2f}"`.

On the log scale the criterion stays in its own unit, percent. A prediction interval is calculated on the log scale and transformed back. It keeps its 95 % coverage, because the probability that ln y lies between two values is the probability that y lies between their antilogs. It is asymmetric in percentage points, further above the predicted value than below it. At the least favourable NOR combination for acidic variants, for example, the interval runs `{python} fx(WCA['predicted'] - WCA['pi_low'])` points below the predicted value and `{python} fx(WCA['pi_high'] - WCA['predicted'])` points above it. The predicted value of a log-scale model is the median of the output, its geometric mean, and not its arithmetic mean. The prediction limits, which decide the verdict against a criterion, are not affected by that.

A selected model is adequate for prediction under PCP-003 §7 when all of the following hold. The first four restate the criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2.

a. The model F-test. The F-test of the model is significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"`.
b. The lack-of-fit test. Lack of fit against pure error is not significant at α = `{python} f"{LOF_A:g}"`.
c. The limit on overfitting. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} fx(GAPMAX)`. Predicted R² comes from the prediction error sum of squares (PRESS).
d. The criterion on residuals and influential runs. A regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values, and a regression of the residuals on the run order, each show no slope significant at α = `{python} f"{RES_A:g}"`. No run has a Cook's distance above the median of the F distribution with p and n − p degrees of freedom, the F median, where p is the number of parameters of the model and n the number of runs. A run with a Cook's distance above `{python} f"{COOKF:g}"`/n, which is `{python} fx(COOK_LIM, 3)` for the `{python} N_ALL` runs of the models, is examined by deleting it and repeating the analysis. The augmentation runs continue the order of the planned runs.
e. The normality criterion. The normal quantile plot of the residuals shows no departure from normality.

Each run above `{python} f"{COOKF:g}"`/n was deleted in turn and the model selection repeated. Each attribute was then judged over the NOR again, and its NOR-propagated PARs and the design space were computed again. The models that do not meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs were used for the ranges and the design space, with each residual trend sized against the criterion of its output (PD-003-04).

Other models may have an AICc within `{python} f"{NEAR_D:g}"` units of the lowest and fit the data almost as well [@burnham2002]. They were computed for every output, and @sec-near states where they differ from the selected model.

Each output is judged against its intermediate acceptance criterion at manufacturing scale. A quality attribute is judged on the exact 95 % prediction interval of a single run at each of the `{python} N_NORCOMB` combinations of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} words(len(FS))` response-surface factors, with the offset applied. The interval comes from the t distribution and includes the uncertainty of the coefficients and the residual, the scatter between runs of the scale-down model. It does not include variation between manufacturing batches beyond that scatter, and it does not include the uncertainty of the offset, which the qualification handles (@sec-sdm). It is two-sided, so each of its ends is a one-sided 97.5 % limit. A two-sided criterion is judged at both ends. In this report the verdict over the NOR of an attribute means whether it meets its criterion at all `{python} N_NORCOMB` combinations.

The PARs were computed as PCMP-001 §6.4 defines them. The set-point analysis holds the other factors at their set-points, scans the factor across its range studied at `{python} D.PAR_GRID_SETPOINT` points, and takes the contiguous range around the set-point over which the mean prediction meets the criterion. The NOR-propagated analysis scans the factor at `{python} D.PAR_GRID` points. At each point it draws `{python} f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"` settings of the other factors, each from a normal distribution centred on its set-point with a standard deviation equal to the width of its NOR divided by `{python} f"{D.NOR_SD_DIVISOR:g}"`, clipped to the range studied. PCMP-001 §6.4 takes that standard deviation as the routine variation of the parameter. Each simulated run takes its own coefficients from their estimated distribution and its own residual. The 2.5th percentile of the simulated runs must not fall below a lower limit, and the 97.5th percentile must not exceed an upper limit. The NOR-propagated PAR is the one that supports a claim.

The design space was evaluated on a grid of `{python} DS_N_AXIS` evenly spaced points along each response-surface factor, `{python} f"{DSG['n_points']:,}"` points in all (@sec-design-space). Capability at commercial scale was estimated from the integrated model of the train, which runs `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` simulated batches through every step with each parameter drawn as in the NOR-propagated analysis (PCMP-001 §6.5). Cpk is computed against the drug substance criterion, as the lower of the two one-sided indices for a two-sided criterion. The same simulation gives the probability that the drug substance falls outside its criterion, as the count of simulated batches outside it and as the tail probability of a normal distribution with the simulated mean and standard deviation.

PCP-003 §6.4 gives no test for a univariate difference. Each univariate parameter was judged on the difference between the mean of its two runs at the high end and the mean of its two runs at the low end of the range studied, by a t-test against the pooled standard deviation of the duplicate runs (PD-003-05, `{python} UV_DF` degrees of freedom), at the level of α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` that PCMP-001 §6.2 sets for a single test. The results of the osmolality study were fitted by a straight line in osmolality, coded −1, 0 and +1 at the NOR low, the set-point and the NOR high. Each level was judged on the fitted mean and on the 95 % prediction interval of a single run at manufacturing scale.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space {#sec-factors}

@tbl-params lists the `{python} words(len(PRM))` parameters of the step with the set-point, the NOR, the range studied, the study type and the class assigned in @sec-classification. The set-point is the target of commercial operation, and the NOR is the band within which routine operation holds the parameter. The range studied is the knowledge space of this characterization. No NOR and no set-point of this step was changed at Version 2.0.

## Screening design {#sec-screening-design}

The screening study S-BRX-SCR varied the `{python} words(len(SFS))` multivariate parameters in a resolution V half fraction of the two-level factorial design, with `{python} N_SCR - NC_SCR` factorial runs and `{python} words(NC_SCR)` centre points, `{python} N_SCR` runs in all. At resolution V every main effect and every two-factor interaction can be estimated clear of the others, and each is aliased only with interactions of three factors or more. The runs were made in randomized order under SOP-1002. The design carries no squared term, so it can detect curvature but cannot attribute it to a factor. Appendix A gives the settings and the results.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm-design}

The response-surface study S-BRX-RSM varied `{python} join_and([pname(k) for k in FS])` in a face-centred central composite design. The design has `{python} N_FACT` factorial runs, `{python} N_AXIAL` axial runs at the centres of the faces of the design cube and `{python} words(NC_RSM)` centre points, `{python} N_PLAN` runs in all. Each factor is run at three levels. Osmolality was held at its set-point in every run. PCP-003 §6.3 planned this subset of factors. It also requires the factors carried into the design to be those that the screening identifies as active, with the design amended before execution if the subset differs. Osmolality was active in the screening (@sec-screening) and was not carried forward (PD-003-07). Appendix B gives the settings and the results.

The design was augmented with `{python} N_AUG` runs under INV-002, in a D-optimal augmentation run as a second block, the study S-BRX-AUG (`{python} win('S-BRX-AUG')`) [@fedorov1972]. INV-002 decided its rule on `{python} MA['decided']`, after the results of the planned runs were known and before any augmentation run was made. A failing model of an attribute of the drug substance specification on which the planned design shows an effect is augmented, and every other failing model is refitted. The number of runs is the smallest augmentation found in INV-002 to give a probability of at least `{python} fx(MA['assurance'])` that the full quadratic models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in AUGR])` meet the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting. The augmentation is the discrepancy PD-003-02, and Appendix B gives its runs.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate-design}

The univariate study S-BRX-UNI (`{python} win('S-BRX-UNI')`) assessed `{python} join_and(['dissolved oxygen', 'initial viable cell concentration', 'basal medium concentration', 'nutrient feed-1 volume'])` one at a time. Each parameter was run at the low and the high end of its range studied with every other parameter at its set-point, and the harvest was assayed for the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` responses and the two impurities. PCP-003 §6.4 plans one run at each end. Duplicate runs were made at each end, `{python} len(UV)` runs in all, to measure the variation between runs within the study (PD-003-05). The set-point reference of the study is the scale-down runs of the qualification study. This design cannot show whether the effect of one of these parameters depends on the level of another [@ichq8], so the range it supports is conditioned on the other parameters being at their set-points.

## Osmolality study {#sec-osm-design}

The osmolality study S-BRX-OSM (`{python} win('S-BRX-OSM')`) ran osmolality at its NOR low, set-point and NOR high. The `{python} words(len(FS))` response-surface parameters were held at the combination of NOR settings least favourable for acidic variants, culture pH at `{python} pv('pH', WCA['settings']['pH'])`, culture temperature at `{python} pv('temperature', WCA['settings']['temperature'])`, culture duration at `{python} pv('duration', WCA['settings']['duration'])` and pCO2 at `{python} pv('co2', WCA['settings']['co2'])`. The study was made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, after the screening and response-surface results were known, and it is recorded as the discrepancy PD-003-01. Each level had `{python} words(OSM_N)` runs, the smallest number for which the straight-line prediction at the NOR high has a standard error of at most `{python} f"{OSM_SE:g}"` times the standard deviation between runs.

## Execution of the studies {#sec-chronology}

@tbl-chronology gives the execution window of each study. Every study of PCP-003 ran in the scale-down bioreactor system whose pCO2 probe is EQ-BRX-205, and each window closed before the next calibration of that probe was due on `{python} PROBE_DUE`. The univariate study started on `{python} S0('S-BRX-UNI')`, before the response-surface study started on `{python} S0('S-BRX-RSM')`, against the sequence of PCP-003 §11 (PD-003-10). The records of the osmolality and augmentation studies name no equipment and state no calibration status of the pCO2 probe (PD-003-12). Host cell protein and DNA were measured in the clarified harvest of every run of the screening, response-surface and univariate designs. They were not measured on the qualification runs, on the augmentation runs or in the osmolality study.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility {#sec-centre}

@tbl-centre gives the mean, the standard deviation and the coefficient of variation of the centre points of both designs. These replicates carry the variation between runs of the scale-down model and of the methods, and they are the pure error of the lack-of-fit test. High mannose is the least precise attribute at the centre point in both designs, with a coefficient of variation of `{python} pct(CV_HM_S)` in the screening design and `{python} pct(CV_HM_R)` in the response-surface design. That is several times the precision of the glycan map, `{python} pct(float(AMV3010.precision_pct))` of the result (Appendix D), so most of the variation in high mannose comes from the culture. The standard deviation of galactosylation at the centre point is `{python} fx(SD_GA_R)` points in the response-surface design against `{python} fx(SD_GA_S)` in the screening design. The larger value enters the lack-of-fit test of the galactosylation model as pure error, which is one reason why that test has the highest p-value of the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` models (@sec-models).

```{python}
#| output: asis

    _body.append([ANAME[_r], str(int(_a["n"])), T.num(_a["Mean"]), T.num(_a["SD"]), f"{_a['%CV']:.1f}",
                  str(int(_b["n"])), T.num(_b["Mean"]), T.num(_b["SD"]), f"{_b['%CV']:.1f}"])
CTable(header=_hdr, body=_body, align="lrrrrrrrr",
       caption="Mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation of the centre points of the two designs, "

```

## Screening: factor effects {#sec-screening}

@tbl-screening lists the effects significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` for each attribute, as the change in the attribute across the range studied of the factor. The screening models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in SCR_NSIG_MODEL])` have no significant model F-test (p `{python} pfmt(SCRF['afucosylation']['p'])` and p `{python} pfmt(SCRF['high_mannose']['p'])`), so their individual effects identify candidates and no more. No attribute shows significant curvature in the screening design, with lack-of-fit p-values from `{python} fx(SCR_LOF_MIN, 3)` to `{python} fx(SCR_LOF_MAX, 3)`, but with `{python} words(SDF_PE)` degrees of freedom for pure error that test detects only a large curvature.

pCO2 has the largest effect on acidic variants, which fall by `{python} fx(abs(eff('acidic_variants', LTR['co2'])))` points from the low to the high end of its range. A higher culture pH also lowers acidic variants, and a higher culture temperature raises them. Culture duration has the largest effect on galactosylation, a fall of `{python} fx(abs(eff('galactosylation', LTR['duration'])))` points, and the interaction of culture pH with culture duration is nearly as large and of opposite sign. A higher pCO2 and a higher culture pH lower galactosylation, and a higher culture temperature raises it. A higher culture pH and a longer culture raise aggregate, by `{python} fx(eff('aggregates_hmw', LTR['pH']))` and `{python} fx(eff('aggregates_hmw', LTR['duration']))` points. A higher culture pH raises high mannose and a higher culture temperature lowers it. Afucosylation falls with a longer culture, and its interactions of culture pH with culture duration and with pCO2 are significant.

A higher osmolality lowers galactosylation by `{python} fx(abs(eff('galactosylation', OSM_L)))` points (p `{python} pfmt(pef('galactosylation', OSM_L))`) and acidic variants by `{python} fx(abs(eff('acidic_variants', OSM_L)))` points (p `{python} pfmt(pef('acidic_variants', OSM_L))`) across its range, and its interactions with `{python} join_and([_short(INV_LTR[[c for c in t if c != OSM_L][0]]) for t in OSM_INT_GA])` are significant for galactosylation. Under PCP-003 §6.3 osmolality should therefore have been carried into the response-surface design, with the design amended before execution. It was not (PD-003-07). The osmolality study later measured its effect at the least favourable NOR combination for acidic variants (@sec-osmolality).

Screening run 4 ran below its design setting of pCO2, because the pCO2 probe read high (study event DEV-003-01). Appendix A shows the run at its design setting, and the analysis uses its recorded setting of `{python} pv('co2', R4_REC)`. The set of significant effects in @tbl-screening is the same with the run at its design setting (@sec-dev-01). The response-surface model re-estimates the effects of the `{python} words(len(FS))` factors carried forward, in a design without aliases, and it is the model from which the ranges and the design space are predicted.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_neg = lambda v: T.num(v).replace("-", "−")
_cap = lambda s_: s_ if (s_[:1] == "p" and s_[1:2].isupper()) else cap1(s_)
_rows = []
for _r in RESPS:
    _e = SCRE[_r]
    for _, _x in _e[_e["p-value"] < ALPHA].iterrows():
        _rows.append([ANAME[_r], _cap(tname(lt_term(_x["Term"]))), _neg(_x["Effect"]), p3(_x["p-value"])])
_scr = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Term", "Effect", "p-value"])
T.frame(_scr, f"Effects significant at α = {ALPHA:g} in the screening design. The effect is the change in the "
        "attribute across the range studied of the factor, as measured in the scale-down model.",
        "tbl-screening", merge=["Attribute"], header={"Effect": "Effect\n(points)"},
        align=["P{3.6cm}", "P{5.8cm}", "r", "r"]).show()
```

## Response-surface models {#sec-rsm}

### Selected models and their adequacy {#sec-models}

@tbl-models gives the selected model of each attribute on all `{python} N_ALL` runs. The raw scale is used for `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RAWR])`, and the log scale for `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in LOGR])`. For afucosylation the Box-Cox interval excludes both 0 and 1, so the rule keeps the raw scale although the profile does not support it either (@sec-residuals). Every selected model meets the model F-test (p < 0.001 for every model), the lack-of-fit test (p from `{python} fx(P_LOF_MIN, 3)` to `{python} fx(P_LOF_MAX, 3)`) and the limit on overfitting, with predicted R² at most `{python} fx(GAP_MAX, 3)` below R² against the limit of `{python} fx(GAPMAX)`.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _r in RESPS:
    _f = FIT[_r]
    _bc = _f["boxcox"]
    _rows.append([ANAME[_r], "log" if _r in LOGR else "raw",
                  f"{_bc['lambda']:.2f} ({_bc['lo']:.2f} to {_bc['hi']:.2f})".replace("-", "−"),
                  str(len(_f["names"])), f"{_f['R2']:.3f}", f"{_f['adjR2']:.3f}", f"{_f['predR2']:.3f}",
                  f"{_f['gap']:.3f}", p3(_f["p"]), p3(_f["p_lof"])])
_mt = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Scale", "Box-Cox λ (95 % interval)", "Terms", "R²", "Adj. R²",
                                   "Pred. R²", "R² minus pred. R²", "F-test p", "Lack of fit p"])
T.frame(_mt, f"Selected response-surface models of the production bioreactor on all {N_ALL} runs, against the "
        "model F-test, the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting.", "tbl-models",
        header={"Box-Cox λ (95 % interval)": "Box-Cox λ\n(95 % interval)", "R² minus pred. R²": "R² minus\npred. R²",
                "Lack of fit p": "Lack of\nfit p", "F-test p": "F-test\np", "Adj. R²": "Adj.\nR²", "Pred. R²": "Pred.\nR²"},
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "l", "P{2.5cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Terms are counted without the intercept and the block term. Adj. R², adjusted R². Pred. R², "
                    "predicted R² from PRESS. The model scale is the log scale where the 95 % interval of the Box-Cox "
                    "exponent λ contains 0 and excludes 1, and the raw scale otherwise.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

At the set-points, the selected models of afucosylation and acidic variants predict `{python} pct(CBIAS['afucosylation']['pred'], 2)` and `{python} pct(CBIAS['acidic_variants']['pred'], 2)` in the scale-down model. The means of the `{python} words(CBIAS['afucosylation']['n'])` centre points of the response-surface design are `{python} pct(CBIAS['afucosylation']['mean'], 2)` and `{python} pct(CBIAS['acidic_variants']['mean'], 2)`, with standard errors of `{python} fx(CBIAS['afucosylation']['se'])` and `{python} fx(CBIAS['acidic_variants']['se'])` points. The lack-of-fit test is not significant for either model. At manufacturing scale the model of acidic variants predicts `{python} pct(SP_MFG['acidic_variants'], 2)` at the set-point, against a geometric mean of `{python} pct(SDM['acidic_variants']['mean_m'], 2)` in the manufacturing batches of the qualification. For acidic variants the difference lies in the unfavourable direction, because a model that predicts too high near the set-point overstates the distance to the lower limit. The predicted median at the least favourable NOR combination lies `{python} fx(WCA['predicted'] - ACC['acidic_variants'][0])` points above the lower limit, less than either difference at the set-point. If the model overstates acidic variants there by the same factor as at the centre points, the median at that combination is about `{python} pct(WCA_BIASED, 2)`, below the lower limit (@sec-criteria-results).

@tbl-reeval-bioreactor sets the plan's full quadratic model, fitted on the raw scale to the planned runs and to all runs with a block term, beside the model used. On the planned runs the full quadratic models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in AUGR])` exceed the limit on overfitting, which is why the design was augmented. On all runs the full quadratic model of acidic variants meets the limit, but that of high mannose still exceeds it, with predicted R² `{python} fx(HM_FULLA_GAP, 2)` below R². The selected model of high mannose meets the limit, and the full quadratic model that the plan prescribes would leave high mannose without an adequate model on all runs.

### Residual patterns and influential runs {#sec-residuals}

The selected models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RI_PASS])` meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs, and those of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RI_FAIL])` do not (@tbl-crit4). For these two the absolute residuals rise with the predicted value, with a slope significant at `{python} join_and([f"p {pfmt(RI[r]['p_spread'])} for {OUT[r]}" for r in SPREAD])`. No model shows a trend with the run order, and the lowest p-value of that test is `{python} fx(P_ORD_MIN, 3)`. No run has a Cook's distance above the F median of its model, which lies between `{python} fx(min(F_LIM), 3)` and `{python} fx(max(F_LIM), 3)` for these models. Every model has at least one run with a Cook's distance above 4/n = `{python} fx(COOK_LIM, 3)`. Across the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` models there are `{python} N_FLAG` such cases, on `{python} len(FLAG_RUNS)` different runs.

Each of these runs was deleted in turn and the model selection repeated. For every attribute and every deleted run, the model selected without the run met the model F-test, the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting, every attribute kept its verdict over the NOR, and every NOR-propagated PAR still contained the NOR. The share of the region studied that lies inside the design space ranged from `{python} pct(100 * min(DS_DEL))` to `{python} pct(100 * max(DS_DEL))`, against `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])` with all runs. The same model was selected in `{python} N_FLAG_SAME` of the `{python} N_FLAG` cases. For afucosylation, `{python} INFL_CHG['afucosylation'][0]`. For high mannose, `{python} INFL_CHG['high_mannose'][0]`. For acidic variants, `{python} join_and(INFL_CHG['acidic_variants'])`.

```{python}

    _rows.append([ANAME[_r], p3(_ri["p_spread"]), p3(_ri["p_order"]), f"{_ri['cook_max']:.3f} ({_ri['cook_run']})",
                  f"{_ri['f_limit']:.3f}", ", ".join(str(_x["run"]) for _x in INFL[_r]),
                  "met" if _ri["met"] else "not met"])
_c4 = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Spread p", "Order p", "Largest Cook's distance (run)", "F median",
                                   "Runs above 4/n", "Verdict"])

        "and influential runs.", "tbl-crit4",
        header={"Spread p": "Spread\np", "Order p": "Order\np",

                    "p and n − p degrees of freedom, where p is the number of parameters of the model.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Each residual trend was sized against the criterion of its attribute, on the residual standard deviation in the lower and the upper half of the predicted values. For galactosylation it is `{python} fx(SPRD['galactosylation']['sd_lo'])` points in the lower half and `{python} fx(SPRD['galactosylation']['sd_hi'])` points in the upper half. The rise that the slope detects therefore does not show as a difference between the halves, and both are small against the width of the criterion, `{python} f"{ACC['galactosylation'][1] - ACC['galactosylation'][0]:g}"` points. For acidic variants it is `{python} fx(SPRD['acidic_variants']['sd_lo'], 3)` in the lower half and `{python} fx(SPRD['acidic_variants']['sd_hi'], 3)` in the upper half, on the log scale. With the standard deviation of the half in which each prediction lies, both attributes keep their verdict over the NOR. For acidic variants the lowest prediction limit moves from `{python} pct(WCA['pi_low'], 2)` to `{python} pct(SPRD['acidic_variants']['lo'], 2)`, still below the lower limit. Afucosylation, whose Box-Cox profile rejects the raw scale and whose slope is not significant (p `{python} pfmt(RI['afucosylation']['p_spread'])`), has a residual standard deviation of `{python} fx(SPRD['afucosylation']['sd_lo'])` points in the lower half and `{python} fx(SPRD['afucosylation']['sd_hi'])` in the upper half. Judged with the standard deviation of each half, it still meets its criterion across the NOR, with prediction limits from `{python} pct(SPRD['afucosylation']['lo'], 2)` to `{python} pct(SPRD['afucosylation']['hi'], 2)`.

The normal quantile plots of the residuals in @fig-diag-afucosylation to @fig-diag-aggregates show no departure from normality, so the normality criterion is met.

### Effects of the parameters {#sec-effects}

The coefficients of the selected models are in coded units, so each measures the change from the set-point to the end of the range of its factor. Appendix C gives the coefficient tables of afucosylation, galactosylation, high mannose and aggregate, and @tbl-coef-acidic and @tbl-anova-acidic those of acidic variants, the attribute nearest its limit. @tbl-effect-size states each main effect as the change it causes across the range studied, at manufacturing scale with the other factors at their set-points, against the width of the criterion.

PCP-003 §7 calls an effect practically important when that change is large relative to the width of the criterion, and PCMP-001 §7.7 asks for the size of an effect beside its significance. Neither sets a threshold. @tbl-effect-size describes a change of a fifth of the width or more as large, of a tenth to a fifth as moderate and of less than a tenth as small. These bands are a judgement of this report, and no class rests on them (@sec-classification). Only for acidic variants do the effects bring the attribute to its limit within the NOR. There a higher pCO2 and a higher culture pH each lower acidic variants, and the PARs of these two parameters end just above their NOR highs (@sec-par-table).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _e in EFF:
    _rows.append([ANAME[_e["resp"]], _cap(_short(_e["factor"])), f"{_e['d']:.2f}".replace("-", "−"),
                  f"{_e['d_nor']:.2f}".replace("-", "−"), f"{_e['width']:.3g}", f"{_e['share']:.1f}", BAND(_e["share"])])
_ef = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Parameter", "Change over the range studied", "Change over the NOR",
                                   "Criterion width", "Share of the width (%)", "Size"])
T.frame(_ef, "Main effects of the selected models against the width of each criterion, at manufacturing scale "
        "with the other factors at their set-points.", "tbl-effect-size", merge=["Attribute"],
        header={"Change over the range studied": "Change over the\nrange studied", "Change over the NOR": "Change over\nthe NOR",
                "Criterion width": "Criterion\nwidth", "Share of the width (%)": "Share of the\nwidth (%)"},
        align=["P{2.6cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Main effects only, for the parameters in each selected model. Changes and widths in percentage points. "
                    "Size, the report's own bands: large from a fifth of the width, moderate from a tenth, small below a "
                    "tenth. The aggregate criterion has an upper limit only, and its width is taken from 0.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Afucosylation falls as culture duration, culture pH, culture temperature and pCO2 rise. The interaction of culture pH with culture duration is as large as the main effect of culture duration and of opposite sign. At the low end of the pH range a longer culture lowers afucosylation by `{python} fx(abs(DUR_AF_LO))` points across the range of culture duration, and at the high end of the pH range it changes it by `{python} fx(abs(DUR_AF_HI))` points. The squared term of culture pH is negative, so with the other factors at their set-points afucosylation is highest inside the pH range and falls toward both ends.

Galactosylation falls with culture duration, pCO2 and culture pH, and rises with culture temperature. Culture pH changes the size of each of these effects. Across the range of culture duration galactosylation falls by `{python} fx(abs(DUR_GA_LO), 1)` points at the low end of the pH range and by `{python} fx(abs(DUR_GA_HI), 1)` points at the high end. Across the range of pCO2 it falls by `{python} fx(abs(CO2_GA_LO), 1)` and `{python} fx(abs(CO2_GA_HI), 1)` points. Across the range of culture temperature it rises by `{python} fx(TMP_GA_LO, 1)` points at the low end of the pH range and by `{python} fx(TMP_GA_HI, 1)` points at the high end.

High mannose rises with culture pH, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('high_mannose', 'pH'))` across its range, and falls with culture temperature, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('high_mannose', 'temperature'))`. The small interaction of the two is significant. Neither culture duration nor pCO2 is in the model.

Acidic variants fall with pCO2, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('acidic_variants', 'co2'))` across its range, and with culture pH, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('acidic_variants', 'pH'))`. They rise with culture temperature, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('acidic_variants', 'temperature'))`. The main effect of culture duration is a factor of `{python} fx(fold('acidic_variants', 'duration'))` and is not significant (p `{python} pfmt(P_DUR_AC)`). It stays in the model because the interaction of culture pH with culture duration does. The interaction of culture pH with culture temperature is significant. Of the terms of this model, only `{python} term_names(ACID_COMMON)` are carried by every model whose AICc lies within `{python} f"{NEAR_D:g}"` units of the lowest (@sec-near).

Aggregate rises with culture pH, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('aggregates_hmw', 'pH'))` across its range, and with culture duration, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('aggregates_hmw', 'duration'))`. The interaction of the two is negative on the log scale, so a longer culture multiplies aggregate by less at high pH than at low pH. The squared term of culture pH is negative, so the rise with pH flattens toward the top of the range. Neither culture temperature nor pCO2 is in the model.

@fig-contours shows the response surfaces over culture pH and culture duration, with culture temperature and pCO2 at their set-points. The surfaces are predictions of the scale-down model before the offset, and for a log-scale attribute they show the median.

```{python}
        _d[_c] = _d[_c].map(lambda v: f"{v:.4f}".replace("-", "−"))
```

### What the augmentation changed {#sec-augmentation}

The `{python} N_AUG` augmentation runs were added after the results of the planned runs were known, and every selected model is fitted to them. Their pCO2 settings rest on a probe whose calibration status the record does not give (PD-003-12).

On the `{python} N_PLAN` planned runs alone, the selected models meet the model F-test, the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting for every attribute. Their NOR-propagated PARs for acidic variants end at pH `{python} APA_TXT['pH'].split('–')[1]` for culture pH, start at `{python} APA_TXT['temperature'].split('–')[0]` °C for culture temperature and end at `{python} APA_TXT['co2'].split('–')[1]` mmHg for pCO2, so none of the three contains the NOR. At the least favourable NOR combination the predicted median is `{python} pct(ALT_PLAN['wc']['predicted'], 2)` and the lower prediction limit `{python} pct(ALT_PLAN['wc']['pi_low'], 2)`, and the design space covers `{python} pct(100 * ALT_PLAN['ds'])` of the region studied. With the plan's full quadratic model on all `{python} N_ALL` runs, the PAR of pCO2 ends at `{python} D._par_str(CO2_FULL).split('–')[1]` mmHg, the design space covers `{python} pct(100 * ALT_FULL['ds'])`, and high mannose exceeds the limit on overfitting. That every PAR contains the NOR, and that the design space covers `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])`, therefore rests on the augmentation runs and on the model selection together.

A model selected on the same runs on which it is judged passes an optimistic check, and the augmentation runs are an independent one. @tbl-augcheck shows how well the models selected on the planned runs predict the augmentation runs. The models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in POOR])` predict them poorly, with a root mean square error of prediction `{python} fx(AUGC.loc['high_mannose', 'rmsep'] / AUGC.loc['high_mannose', 'rmse_model'], 1)` and `{python} fx(AUGC.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'rmsep'] / AUGC.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'rmse_model'], 1)` times their residual standard deviation. For aggregate only `{python} AUG_IN_AGG` of the `{python} AUG_N` augmentation runs fall inside their 95 % prediction intervals, so the single-run intervals of aggregate understate the scatter between runs. That limits the verdict of aggregate over the NOR. The block term is not significant for any attribute (p ≥ `{python} fx(min(AUGC.block_p), 2)`), so a shift between the two blocks does not explain the misses.

### Near-equivalent models {#sec-near}

Besides the selected models, `{python} N_NEAR_OTHERS` models have an AICc within `{python} f"{NEAR_D:g}"` units of the lowest, `{python} join_and([('none' if NEAR_OTHERS[r] == 0 else str(NEAR_OTHERS[r])) + ' for ' + OUT[r] for r in RESPS])`. Each of them meets the model F-test, the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting, gives every attribute the same verdict over the NOR as the selected model and leaves the scale-down model qualified. They differ from the selected model by `{python} words(min(NEAR_DIFF))` to `{python} words(max(NEAR_DIFF))` terms. For afucosylation some carry `{python} term_names(NEAR['afucosylation']['vary'])`, for high mannose `{python} term_names(NEAR['high_mannose']['vary'])`, and for aggregate `{python} term_names(NEAR['aggregates_hmw']['vary'])`. For acidic variants they share only `{python} term_names(ACID_COMMON)`.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

@tbl-univariate gives every result of the univariate study for the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` attributes, and @tbl-uni-effects the difference between the two ends of each range, both at manufacturing scale. Every result meets its criterion. The half-width of the 95 % confidence interval in @tbl-uni-effects is the precision of each comparison. For galactosylation, for example, a difference of `{python} fx(UV_HW['galactosylation'], 1)` points between the two ends of a range is detected about half the time, and a difference of `{python} fx(DET80, 1)` points with a probability of 80 %.

Acidic variants are `{python} fx(UIV_D_MFG)` points higher at the high end of the initial viable cell concentration than at the low end, with a 95 % confidence interval of ± `{python} fx(UIV_HW_MFG)` points (p `{python} pfmt(UIV['p'])`). It is the only significant result among the `{python} N_UV_TESTS` univariate tests of @tbl-uni-effects. Each was made at the level that PCMP-001 §6.2 sets for a single test, at which about one test in twenty with no real effect gives a significant result, so about `{python} fx(EXP_FP, 1)` such results are expected among them by chance. No correction for the number of tests is applied, because none was set before the result. No effect of dissolved oxygen, basal medium concentration or nutrient feed-1 volume was detected on any attribute, at the precision given in @tbl-uni-effects, and no effect of the initial viable cell concentration was detected on any other attribute.

PCP-003 §6.4 carries a univariate parameter into a multivariate study when it shows an effect on a quality attribute that the mechanism given in PCP-003 §4.3 does not account for. That mechanism, restated in @sec-platform, expects the initial viable cell concentration to change the number of viable cells and the titre, and no quality attribute. One route to acidic variants would be the time the antibody spends in the culture fluid at culture temperature, since a culture that starts at a higher cell concentration makes its antibody earlier. That route does not account for the effect. Culture duration sets the time in the culture fluid most directly, and it has no detectable main effect on acidic variants, in the screening design (p `{python} pfmt(P_DUR_AC_SCR)`) or in the response-surface model (p `{python} pfmt(P_DUR_AC)`). The parameter should therefore have been carried into a multivariate study and the plan amended, and that was not done (PD-003-11).

A straight line between the two ends of the range puts acidic variants `{python} fx(abs(IV_NORLO_MFG))` points lower at the NOR low of the initial viable cell concentration than at its set-point, with the other parameters at their set-points. The response-surface and osmolality studies ran at the set-point of this parameter, so the verdict over the NOR in @sec-criteria-results does not include its effect. Added to the least favourable combination of the `{python} words(len(FS))` response-surface parameters, on the assumption that the effect does not depend on them, it would move the predicted median from `{python} pct(WCA['predicted'], 2)` to `{python} pct(WCA_IV_MED, 2)`, below the lower limit, and the lower prediction limit from `{python} pct(WCA['pi_low'], 2)` to `{python} pct(WCA_IV_LO, 2)`. The acceptance of the acidic-variant risk in @sec-criteria-results covers this combination on the same grounds. Acidic variants at harvest are to be trended against the initial viable cell concentration of each production batch, so that a false positive is found out.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_lab = {**{_r: ANAME[_r] for _r in RESPS}, "harvest_hcp_ng_mg": "Host cell protein (ng/mg)",
        "harvest_dna_pg_mg": "DNA (pg/mg)"}
_kf_ = lambda r: (float(D.to_mfg(UO, r, 1.0) - D.to_mfg(UO, r, 0.0)) if r in RESPS else 1.0)
_fm = lambda v, r: (s3(v) if r.startswith("harvest") else T.num(v))
_rows = []
for _k in UNI:
    for _r in UVR:
        _s = UVS[(_k, _r)]
        _lo, _hi = (float(D.to_mfg(UO, _r, _s["lo"])), float(D.to_mfg(UO, _r, _s["hi"]))) if _r in RESPS else (_s["lo"], _s["hi"])
        _rows.append([PRM[_k].name, _lab[_r], _fm(_lo, _r), _fm(_hi, _r), _fm(_hi - _lo, _r).replace("-", "−"),
                      _fm(_s["hw"] * _kf_(_r), _r), p3(_s["p"])])
_ue = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Parameter", "Attribute", "Mean, low end", "Mean, high end", "High minus low",
                                   "95 % CI half-width", "p-value"])
T.frame(_ue, "Difference between the high and the low end of each univariate parameter. The five modelled attributes "
        "at manufacturing scale, host cell protein and DNA in the clarified harvest as measured.", "tbl-uni-effects",
        merge=["Parameter"],
        header={"Mean, low end": "Mean,\nlow end", "Mean, high end": "Mean,\nhigh end", "High minus low": "High\nminus low",
                "95 % CI half-width": "95 % CI\nhalf-width"},
        align=["P{2.8cm}", "P{4.0cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"Each mean is of two runs. The confidence interval uses the pooled standard deviation of the duplicate "
                    f"runs of the study, with {UV_DF} degrees of freedom. The p-value is the same at either scale.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

## Osmolality study {#sec-osmolality}

@tbl-osmolality gives each attribute at the `{python} words(len(OSM_LV))` levels of osmolality, at manufacturing scale, with the other parameters at the combination of NOR settings least favourable for acidic variants. The means in the table are values of the straight line fitted to the `{python} OSM_N * len(OSM_LV)` runs. For acidic variants the line falls by `{python} fx(abs(OSM_CH['acidic_variants']))` points across the NOR of osmolality, but its slope is not significant (p `{python} pfmt(OSM_P['acidic_variants'])`). Its fitted mean lies above the lower limit at the NOR low and at the set-point, and below it at the NOR high, at `{python} pct(OSM_AC_HI['mean'])`. The prediction interval of a single run reaches below the lower limit at every level, as the response-surface model showed at the set-point of osmolality. Afucosylation falls by `{python} fx(abs(OSM_CH['afucosylation']))` points across the NOR, with a significant slope (p `{python} pfmt(OSM_P['afucosylation'])`), and galactosylation by `{python} fx(abs(OSM_CH['galactosylation']))` points (p `{python} pfmt(OSM_P['galactosylation'])`). Every attribute other than acidic variants meets its criterion at every level.

The study therefore shows no significant effect of osmolality on acidic variants at this combination, and the fitted mean at the NOR high is not a finding. It ran at that single combination, with osmolality set by sodium chloride independently of pCO2, so it does not give the interactions of osmolality with the other parameters. Its record names no equipment, so the calibration of the probe that held pCO2 at `{python} pv('co2', WCA['settings']['co2'])` is not documented (PD-003-12). The study was decided after the screening and response-surface results were known.

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mechanism}

Galactosylation falls with culture duration, the direction that the late depletion of UDP-galactose and of the manganese cofactor of the galactosyltransferase predicts (@sec-platform). The fall is much larger at the low end of the pH range than at the high end. A galactosyltransferase whose rate depends on the pH of the Golgi predicts an interaction of culture pH with culture duration, but not its sign. Culture temperature raises galactosylation at high pH and has no effect at low pH.

Afucosylation also falls with culture duration at low pH, and hardly at high pH. The mechanism predicts a rise. A pool weighted toward antibody made late in the culture, when GDP-fucose and the processing capacity of the Golgi have declined, should carry more antibody without core fucose.

A higher pCO2 lowers galactosylation, afucosylation and acidic variants, in each case the direction of a higher culture pH. The mechanism predicts the direction of a lower culture pH, because dissolved carbon dioxide lowers the pH in the cytosol. Osmolality was a factor of the screening design, at `{python} f"{PRM['osmolality'].prange[0]:g}"` and `{python} pv('osmolality', PRM['osmolality'].prange[1])`, set independently of pCO2, and it was held at its set-point in the response-surface design. A rise of osmolality with pCO2 therefore does not explain the direction.

Acidic variants rise with culture temperature, the direction in which a higher temperature speeds deamidation. They fall as culture pH rises, although a higher pH speeds deamidation too. A higher pH would have to lower the sialylated or glycated forms by more than it raises the deamidated ones, and icIEF does not measure the three routes apart.

Aggregate rises with culture pH and with culture duration, the directions that the weaker repulsion between antibody molecules near the isoelectric point and the longer time at temperature predict (@sec-platform). On the log scale the two effects multiply, so aggregate is highest after a long culture at high pH. High mannose rises with culture pH and falls with culture temperature. A warmer culture speeds the processing enzymes of the Golgi, which predicts less high mannose, and the mechanism gives no direction for the pH effect.

The mechanism of @sec-platform therefore does not explain the direction of the effect of culture duration on afucosylation, of pCO2 on galactosylation, afucosylation and acidic variants, or of culture pH on acidic variants, and it does not account for the effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants (@sec-univariate).

For the operation of the step, the attribute nearest its limit is acidic variants at its lower limit. A high culture pH, a high pCO2 and a low culture temperature lower acidic variants. A high osmolality lowered them in the screening design, and a low initial viable cell concentration in the univariate study. Galactosylation approaches its upper limit at low pH, high temperature, short culture and low pCO2, but at the least favourable NOR combination its prediction interval stays `{python} fx(ACC['galactosylation'][1] - WCG['pi_high'], 1)` points below that limit. Routine operation is therefore limited by acidic variants, whose risk @sec-criteria-results accepts and @sec-control mitigates.

# Design space {#sec-design-space}

The design space of this step is the region of the `{python} words(len(FS))` response-surface parameters over which every modelled attribute meets its intermediate acceptance criterion. It is judged on the 95 % prediction interval of a single run at manufacturing scale, as PCMP-001 §6.2 requires. A setting lies inside it when both ends of that interval lie within the criterion of every attribute. Osmolality and the `{python} words(len(UNI))` univariate parameters are held at their set-points, so the design space is conditioned on them, and it is not claimed beyond the ranges studied.

On the grid of `{python} f"{DSG['n_points']:,}"` points, `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])` of the region studied lies inside the design space. Its boundary is set by the lower limit of acidic variants, which excludes `{python} pct(100 * DSG['per_response']['acidic_variants'])` of the grid points. Galactosylation excludes `{python} pct(100 * DSG['per_response']['galactosylation'])` and afucosylation `{python} pct(100 * DSG['per_response']['afucosylation'])`, and high mannose and aggregate exclude none. On the mean prediction in place of the single-run interval, `{python} pct(100 * DSM['fraction'])` of the grid would lie inside. A region drawn on mean predictions gives a single batch at its edge only about an even chance of meeting the criterion (PCMP-001 §6.2).

@fig-design-space shows two planes of the design space in culture pH and pCO2. In the first, culture temperature and culture duration are at their set-points, and `{python} pct(100 * DS_SHARE[0])` of the NOR of culture pH and pCO2, at its corner of high pH and high pCO2, lies outside the design space. In the second, culture temperature is at its NOR low and culture duration at its NOR high, the settings least favourable for acidic variants, and `{python} pct(100 * DS_SHARE[1])` lies outside. The NOR therefore does not lie entirely inside the design space, and @sec-criteria-results gives the decision not to narrow it (PD-003-08).

```{python}
#| label: fig-design-space
#| fig-cap: "Two planes of the design space in culture pH and pCO2, on the 95 % prediction interval of a single run at manufacturing scale. Left, culture temperature and culture duration at their set-points. Right, culture temperature at its NOR low and culture duration at its NOR high. Plain green, every attribute meets its criterion. Hatched red, at least one does not. The rectangle is the NOR and the cross the set-point. The shares outside the design space given in the text come from a grid of 41 by 41 settings over the NOR of culture pH and pCO2."
fig_design_space()
plt.show()
```

Each PAR of @sec-par-table holds while the other parameters vary about their set-points, and the design space holds at every combination of settings at once. As ICH Q8(R2) states, working within the design space is not considered a change from a regulatory filing perspective [@ichq8]. Movement within it is still assessed under the change management of the quality system, and a move outside it is a change [@ichq10]. The design space rests on the scale-down model and is not confirmed at commercial scale at its edges.

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

## Acceptance criteria {#sec-criteria}

Each output is judged against its intermediate acceptance criterion (@tbl-iac). PCMP-001 §7.3 derives the criterion by back-calculation from the drug substance criterion, through the worst case of every downstream step on the platform, with no margin. Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose keep their drug substance criteria, because no downstream step changes them. The upper limit of acidic variants is the drug substance limit less the platform worst case of the increase across low-pH viral inactivation, `{python} fx(float(vi_acid.assumed))` points, which gives `{python} pct(ACC['acidic_variants'][1])`. In the low-pH response-surface design every run at the same hold time gave the same acidic-variant result, so the full quadratic model reproduces the results exactly, cannot be judged against PCMP-001 §7.2, and the platform value stands. The increase applies to the upper limit only. The lower limit is the drug substance limit unchanged, which assumes that no downstream step lowers acidic variants (PCP-003 §12).

The aggregate criterion is the drug substance limit less the aggregate increase across UF/DF, multiplied by the aggregate clearance factor of cation exchange, less the aggregate increase across low-pH viral inactivation. PCMP-001 assumed that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate, and from the platform values alone the criterion is `{python} pct(AGG.iac_high_apriori, 2)`. Verification of the platform worst cases at manufacturing scale changed all three terms (PCMP-001 §7.5). UF/DF raised aggregate within its NOR in the univariate study S-UFDF-UNI2. The one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single run, `{python} fx(float(uf_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))` points, replaced the assumption of no increase (PCR-010). The cation exchange model predicted within its NOR a lowest clearance of `{python} fx(float(cex_agg.predicted_nor))`-fold at manufacturing scale, worse than the platform worst case of `{python} fx(float(cex_agg.assumed))`-fold. The one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single batch there, `{python} fx(float(cex_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))`-fold, replaced the platform value (PCR-007). These two bounds alone would set the criterion at `{python} pct(AGG_TIGHT_ONLY, 2)`. The low-pH viral inactivation model gave a bound of `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))` points for the increase, better than the platform value of `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.assumed))` points, on a model that meets the first three adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 (PCR-006). That bound replaced the platform value too. The criterion in force is `{python} pct(AGG.iac_high, 2)`, stricter than the a priori value. It is computed from the unrounded terms, so the rounded values give `{python} pct((DS_AGG - round(float(uf_agg.predicted_nor_bound95), 2)) * round(float(cex_agg.predicted_nor_bound95), 2) - round(float(vi_agg.predicted_nor_bound95), 2), 2)`. The increase in @tbl-iac is the sum of the two increases, and the UF/DF increase is carried back through the clearance factor of cation exchange.

PCMP-001 §7.5 asks for the risk of the change. The net change is a tightening. No in-process test of aggregate exists at this step, so no batch fails here, and the risk of the tighter criterion falls on the producer at release, where SEC tests aggregate in the drug substance against the limit of `{python} pct(DS_AGG, 1)` and detects an excursion. The widening alone moves the criterion `{python} fx(AGG.iac_high - AGG_TIGHT_ONLY)` points in the direction of a higher risk to the patient. To meet the drug substance limit, cation exchange must clear at least `{python} fx(float(cex_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))`-fold, low-pH viral inactivation must add no more than `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))` points and UF/DF no more than `{python} fx(float(uf_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))` points. At the highest single-run level that the model of this step predicts within the NOR, `{python} pct(AGG_UP, 2)` at manufacturing scale, the drug substance would then carry at most `{python} pct(DS_AGG_EST, 2)`. None of the `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` batches of the integrated model fell outside the aggregate criterion of the drug substance, which puts the probability below `{python} pct(100 * P_UB0, 2)` at one-sided 95 % confidence (@sec-capability).

The widening rests on the bound of the low-pH viral inactivation model, from the `{python} N_VI_RSM` runs of its response-surface design. That model has predicted R² `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.r2_minus_pred_r2), 3)` below R² and a lack-of-fit p-value of `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.p_lack_of_fit), 3)`, and it also meets the criterion on residuals and influential runs. PCR-006 gives the bound and states whether it depends on a single run, as PCMP-001 §7.5 requires. The platform worst case is an increase over a hold of `{python} f"{VIH.prange[1]:g}"` min, while the NOR of the A-Mab hold as characterized ends at `{python} f"{VIH_MAX:g}"` min. At the edges of the range studied, which include the longer hold, A-Mab added up to `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.observed_edge))` points, more than the platform value. The replacement therefore reflects the shorter hold of A-Mab and not a more stable product. It holds for routine manufacture, which is controlled within the hold-time NOR, and the NOR of hold time and temperature in force ends at the same longest hold and highest temperature as the NOR as characterized.

Without the model selection of INV-002 corrective action CA3, the verification would have used the full quadratic models, and the aggregate criterion would be `{python} pct(ACC_WO['aggregates_hmw'][1], 2)`. The low-pH model of acidic variants is an exact fit, which cannot replace the platform value, so the acidic-variant criterion would not change. Judged against that aggregate criterion, aggregate keeps its verdict over the NOR, its PARs and the qualification of its scale-down model.

## Outputs against their criteria over the NOR {#sec-criteria-results}

@tbl-criteria-bioreactor gives each output against its criterion, with the mean predicted at the set-point, its range over the NOR and the limits of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run over the NOR, which decide the verdict. Afucosylation, galactosylation, high mannose and aggregate meet their criteria. Acidic variants do not. At `{python} words(N_FAIL_COMB)` of the `{python} N_NORCOMB` combinations, all with pCO2 at its NOR high, the lower end of the prediction interval falls below `{python} pct(ACC['acidic_variants'][0])`. The least favourable combination is culture pH at its NOR high, culture temperature at its NOR low, culture duration at its NOR high and pCO2 at its NOR high. There the predicted median at manufacturing scale is `{python} pct(WCA['predicted'], 2)` and the prediction interval runs from `{python} pct(WCA['pi_low'], 2)` to `{python} pct(WCA['pi_high'], 2)`. The median lies `{python} fx(WCA['predicted'] - ACC['acidic_variants'][0])` points above the lower limit, less than the bias of the model at the set-point (@sec-models). With the initial viable cell concentration at its NOR low the median would fall to about `{python} pct(WCA_IV_MED, 2)` (@sec-univariate). The upper limit is met at every combination. The verdict is the same with the offset at either end of its interval (@sec-sdm).

```{python}
#| output: asis
# the table below is T.criteria_results("bioreactor").show() with column widths set, so that its numbers stay on
# one line; the builder wraps its group header itself (21f0a49)
_cr = T.criteria_results("bioreactor")
_cr.align = ["P{3.2cm}", "P{2.0cm}", "R{1.5cm}", "R{2.7cm}", "R{2.5cm}", "P{1.6cm}"]
_cr.show()
```

PCP-003 §7 requires the NOR to lie inside the region over which every modelled attribute meets its criterion, and the NOR to be narrowed until it does. Every combination that fails has pCO2 at its NOR high, so the NOR of pCO2 is the one whose narrowing would act on all of them. Some fail with culture pH at its set-point, so narrowing the NOR of culture pH alone would not restore the criterion. The NOR was not narrowed (PD-003-08). It was kept, and the risk accepted as the producer's, on the following grounds.

1. Acidic variants have very low criticality, and their lower limit of `{python} pct(ACC['acidic_variants'][0])` was set from the range of results seen with the product.
2. On all `{python} N_ALL` runs the NOR-propagated PARs contain the NOR, with a margin of `{python} fx(MARG_SD['pH'])` standard deviations of the routine variation of culture pH and `{python} fx(MARG_SD['co2'])` of pCO2 (@sec-par-table). On the planned runs alone they do not (@sec-augmentation), so this ground holds only with the augmentation runs and the model selection.
3. A batch below the limit is detected by the release test of the drug substance against the acidic-variant criterion and does not reach the patient, so the risk of a failure falls on the producer.
4. In the integrated model of the train, `{python} words(int(PO.loc['acidic_variants', 'n_oos']))` of the `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` simulated batches fell outside the acidic-variant criterion (@sec-capability). That model carries no effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants.

At the least favourable combination the fitted mean of the osmolality study lies below the lower limit at the NOR high of osmolality, although its slope is not significant (@sec-osmolality). The same acceptance covers that setting, and it covers the initial viable cell concentration at its NOR low, where the univariate effect would take the median below the lower limit (PD-003-11). For the control strategy that PCMR-001 consolidates, this report recommends a combined alert in the control system, which fires when `{python} ALERT_TXT` at the same time. It also recommends an action limit for acidic variants at harvest of `{python} pct(MIT['action_limit'], 2)`, and the trending of acidic variants against the initial viable cell concentration of each production batch (@sec-control). The release test of the drug substance detects a low result (ground 3).

## PARs {#sec-par-table}

A PAR is a range of a parameter within which the attribute is shown by supportive data to remain acceptable. ICH Q8(R2) defines it with the other parameters kept constant [@ichq8], which is the set-point analysis. The NOR-propagated analysis lets the other parameters vary across their NORs and judges the 95 % interval of the simulated runs, so it is stricter, and it is the PAR that supports a claim (PCMP-001 §6.4). @tbl-par gives both for each of the `{python} words(len(FS))` response-surface parameters and each of the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` attributes, from the selected model of the attribute with the offset applied. Objective 3 requires a PAR where the selected model has a significant term in the parameter, `{python} N_SIGT` of the `{python} N_PAR` combinations. The other `{python} words(N_PAR - N_SIGT)`, `{python} NOSIG_TXT`, have no term in the parameter and are given for information.

Every NOR-propagated PAR contains the NOR, and `{python} N_PAR - len(NARROW)` span the whole range studied. The exceptions are the PARs of culture pH and pCO2 for acidic variants. The PAR of culture pH ends `{python} fx(PMA.loc['pH', 'nor_hi'], 3)` pH units above the NOR high, and the PAR of pCO2 ends `{python} pv('co2', PMA.loc['co2', 'nor_hi'])` above it. Measured in standard deviations of the routine variation of each parameter, the width of its NOR divided by `{python} f"{D.NOR_SD_DIVISOR:g}"` (PCMP-001 §6.4), the margin is `{python} fx(MARG_SD['pH'])` for culture pH and `{python} fx(MARG_SD['co2'])` for pCO2. In the set-point analysis every PAR spans the range studied.

The range carried into the control strategy for each parameter is the intersection of its required PARs (PCP-003 §7, PCMP-001 §7.6). It is pH `{python} INT_TXT['pH']` for culture pH, `{python} INT_TXT['temperature']` °C for culture temperature, `{python} INT_TXT['duration']` days for culture duration and `{python} INT_TXT['co2']` mmHg for pCO2.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rk = {D.RESP_LABEL[_r]: _r for _r in RESPS}
_fk = {PRM[_f].name: _f for _f in FS}
_pt = PT.drop(columns=["Basis", "Char. range"]).copy()
_pt.insert(4, "NOR", [nor_txt(_fk[p_]).replace("pH ", "") if PRM[_fk[p_]].unit == "pH" else f"{PRM[_fk[p_]].nor[0]:g}–{PRM[_fk[p_]].nor[1]:g}"
                      for p_ in _pt["Parameter"]])
_pt.insert(5, "Required", ["yes" if SIGT[(_rk[c_], _fk[p_])] else "no" for c_, p_ in zip(_pt["CQA"], _pt["Parameter"])])
_pt["CQA"] = _pt["CQA"].map({D.RESP_LABEL[_r]: ANAME[_r] for _r in RESPS})
_pt = _pt[["CQA", "Criterion", "Parameter", "Unit", "NOR", "Required", "PAR (set-point)", "PAR (NOR)"]]
T.frame(_pt, "Proven acceptable ranges of the response-surface parameters for each attribute, at manufacturing "
        "scale.", "tbl-par", merge=["CQA", "Criterion"],
        header={"CQA": "Attribute", "PAR (set-point)": "PAR, others\nat set-point", "PAR (NOR)": "PAR, others\nacross NOR",
                "Required": "Required by\nobjective 3"},
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "l", "P{3.4cm}", "l", "l", "l", "l", "l"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Every PAR is computed from the selected model of the attribute. PAR, others at set-point: the mean "
                    "prediction with the other factors at their set-points. PAR, others across NOR: the 95 % interval of "
                    "the simulated runs with the other factors drawn across their NORs, the PAR that supports a claim. "
                    "Required by objective 3: the selected model has a significant term in the parameter. A PAR edge is "
                    "rounded toward the inside of the range, to three significant figures. The range studied of each "
                    "parameter is given in the table of process parameters.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The PAR of pCO2 is a range at the set-point of osmolality, because the response-surface model holds osmolality there. At manufacturing scale a higher pCO2 raises the osmolality as bicarbonate accumulates, and a higher osmolality lowered acidic variants in the screening design (@sec-screening). The PAR of pCO2 for acidic variants therefore does not include the effect of the osmolality rise that comes with it at scale.

@fig-par-afucosylation to @fig-par-aggregates show, for each attribute, the PAR of the parameter with the largest main effect in its selected model. The acceptable region is shaded green, the NOR grey and the criterion dashed. The left panel is the set-point analysis and the right panel the NOR-propagated analysis, with the median and the 95 % interval of the simulated runs. Values are at manufacturing scale.
