## Univariate parameters and osmolality {#sec-par-uni}

The ranges of the `{python} words(len(UNI))` univariate parameters are supported by their own data, with the other parameters at their set-points (PCMP-001 §4). Every result met its criterion at both ends of each range (@tbl-univariate), so the range studied of each parameter is supported for the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` attributes at that condition. For the initial viable cell concentration the support does not extend to the other parameters at their least favourable NOR settings for acidic variants (@sec-univariate). Osmolality has no PAR from a model, because it was not a factor of the response-surface design. The osmolality study supports its NOR for every attribute except acidic variants, at the single combination of the other parameters that it tested, and no range of osmolality beyond its NOR is claimed.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

@tbl-capability gives the capability of the drug substance for the `{python} words(len(KEYS))` attributes that this step sets, from the `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` simulated batches of the integrated model. Each Cpk is judged against the target of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` and the minimum of `{python} fx(CPK_MIN)` of PCMP-001 §7.9. A Cpk between the two is acceptable, and a Cpk below the minimum needs an action in the control strategy.

The integrated model simulates manufacturing-scale batches through the whole train. It does not use the response-surface models of this report, and it applies no scale-down offset, because it simulates manufacturing scale directly. Its drug substance means differ from the predictions of @tbl-criteria-bioreactor, for afucosylation `{python} pct(MC_MEAN['afucosylation'], 2)` against `{python} pct(SP_MFG['afucosylation'], 2)` predicted at the set-point. It draws every parameter of the step as the NOR-propagated analysis does, including osmolality, a higher level of which lowers acidic variants in its process model. It carries no effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants, so the capability does not include the effect found in the univariate study.

```{python}
#| output: asis
def _sci(v):
    """A small positive value as a × 10⁻ⁿ with two significant figures."""
    e = int(math.floor(math.log10(abs(v))))
    sup = str(-e).translate(str.maketrans("0123456789", "⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹"))
    return f"{v / 10 ** e:.1f} × 10⁻{sup}"


def _tail(v):
    return "< 0.01" if v < 0.01 else (f"{v:.0f}" if v >= 10 else f"{v:.2g}")


_rows = []
for _k in KEYS:
    _c, _po = CAPT.loc[_k], PO.loc[_k]
    _cr = f"≤ {_c['acc_high']:g}" if _c["spec_type"] == "upper" else f"{_c['acc_low']:g}–{_c['acc_high']:g}"
    _v = ("above the target" if _c["Cpk"] >= CPK_TARGET else
          "between the minimum and the target" if _c["Cpk"] >= CPK_MIN else "below the minimum")
    _mean, _sd = (DNA_MC_MEAN, DNA_MC_SD) if _k == "residual_dna" else (_c["mean"], _c["sd"])
    _fm = _sci if _k == "residual_dna" else T.num
    _rows.append([ANAME[_k], CRL[_k], _cr, _fm(_mean), _fm(_sd), f"{_c['Cpk']:.2f}", _v,
                  str(int(_po["n_oos"])), _tail(float(_po["ppm_normal"]))])
_cp = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Criticality", "Criterion", "Mean", "SD", "Cpk", "Against PCMP-001",
                                   "Batches outside", "Normal tail (per million)"])
T.frame(_cp, f"Capability of the drug substance for the attributes that the production bioreactor sets, from "
        f"{N_MC:,} batches of the integrated model.", "tbl-capability",
        header={"Criticality": "Criti-\ncality", "Against PCMP-001": "Against the target\nand minimum",
                "Batches outside": "Batches\noutside", "Normal tail (per million)": "Normal tail\n(per million)"},
        align=["P{3.2cm}", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "P{3.0cm}", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"Cpk is the lower of the two one-sided indices for a two-sided criterion. Batches outside, of {N_MC:,}. "
                    "Normal tail, the tail probability of a normal distribution with the simulated mean and standard "
                    f"deviation. Residual DNA in ng per dose of {DOSE_MGKG:g} mg/kg for a {DOSE_KG:g} kg adult.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The Cpk of acidic variants is `{python} fx(ACAP.Cpk)`, between the minimum and the target, and it is limited by the lower limit, with an index of `{python} fx(ACAP.Cpl)` for the lower limit and `{python} fx(ACAP.Cpu)` for the upper. A higher pCO2, a higher culture pH and a lower culture temperature move acidic variants toward the lower limit (@sec-effects). In the simulation `{python} words(int(PO.loc['acidic_variants', 'n_oos']))` of the `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` batches fell outside the criterion. PCMR-001 consolidates this capability with the acceptance of the acidic-variant risk (@sec-criteria-results).

Every other attribute that the step sets has a Cpk above the target, and none of the simulated batches fell outside its criterion. With no simulated batch outside, the probability of a batch outside is below `{python} pct(100 * P_UB0, 2)` at one-sided 95 % confidence. That bound covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated model. Aggregate in the drug substance lies far below its limit, at a mean of `{python} pct(CAPT.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'mean'], 2)`, and it is judged on the prediction interval of a single run over the NOR of this step (@sec-criteria-results) and of the steps after it.

Host cell protein and residual DNA in the drug substance depend on the clearance of the downstream steps, which the integrated model takes from Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008). This step contributes the load, which @sec-sampling gives for information.

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

The parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7 [@amab2009]. A parameter whose variation affects a critical quality attribute within the range studied is a CPP when the risk that it falls outside its acceptable range in operation is not low. It is a WC-CPP when that risk is low, because the parameter is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR. A parameter that affects process performance and no critical quality attribute is a KPP. A parameter with no relevant effect on either is a GPP. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for a relevant effect or a wide PAR, so each class below is argued from the effects found and from the margin between each PAR and its NOR.

- Culture pH is a WC-CPP. It changes all `{python} words(len(CRIT_K))` critical attributes. Its NOR-propagated PARs for the critical attributes span the range studied, and its PAR for acidic variants ends `{python} fx(MARG_SD['pH'])` standard deviations of its routine variation above the NOR high. Base addition holds it at its set-point.
- Culture temperature is a WC-CPP. It changes afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose, and its NOR-propagated PARs span the range studied for every attribute. The vessel jacket holds it.
- pCO2 is a WC-CPP. It changes galactosylation and afucosylation, and its NOR-propagated PARs for these attributes span the range studied. Its PAR for acidic variants, an attribute of very low criticality, ends `{python} fx(MARG_SD['co2'])` standard deviations of its routine variation above the NOR high. The carbon dioxide fraction of the sparge gas holds it.
- Osmolality is a CPP. It lowered galactosylation in the screening design and afucosylation in the osmolality study, both critical attributes. It has no PAR from a model, because it was not a factor of the response-surface design, so its PAR cannot be shown to be wide against its NOR. At its NOR high the fitted mean of acidic variants lies below their lower limit at the least favourable combination of the other parameters, although the slope of the osmolality study is not significant (@sec-osmolality). The risk of operating outside its acceptable range is therefore not shown to be low.
- Culture duration is a WC-CPP. It changes galactosylation, afucosylation and aggregate, and its NOR-propagated PARs span the range studied for every attribute. It is set by the day of harvest.
- Dissolved oxygen is a GPP. No effect was detected on any attribute measured, at the precision of @tbl-uni-effects. The culture is not limited by oxygen at either end of the range studied (@sec-platform), so no effect on growth or titre is expected either.
- The initial viable cell concentration is a KPP. It raised acidic variants, an attribute of very low criticality, by `{python} fx(UIV_D_MFG)` points across its range, in a single significant result that may be a false positive (@sec-univariate), and no effect on a critical attribute was detected. A higher initial concentration brings the culture to its peak cell density earlier and raises the titre (@sec-platform), so it acts on process performance.
- Basal medium concentration is a KPP. No effect was detected on any attribute measured. A higher concentration raises the supply of nutrients, and with it growth and titre (PCP-003 §4.1), so it acts on process performance.
- Nutrient feed-1 volume is a KPP. No effect was detected on any attribute measured. The feed supplies the glucose, amino acids and precursors for growth and titre (@sec-platform), so it acts on process performance. The feed under-delivery of DEV-003-02 left the feed within its NOR (@sec-dev-02).

The classes of the three KPPs rest on their expected effect on growth and titre, which the record does not hold (PD-003-09). The step has `{python} words(NCLS['WC-CPP'])` well-controlled critical process parameters, `{python} words(NCLS['CPP'])` CPP, `{python} words(NCLS['KPP'])` KPPs and `{python} words(NCLS['GPP'])` GPP.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

This step contributes the following elements to the control strategy of A-Mab. The combined alert, the action limit and the trending of items 2 to 4 are recommendations of this report, which PCMR-001 consolidates with those of the other steps.

1. The `{python} words(NCLS['WC-CPP'])` WC-CPPs and the CPP osmolality are held within their NORs by the bioreactor control system. Culture pH is held by base addition, culture temperature by the vessel jacket, pCO2 by the carbon dioxide fraction of the sparge gas, osmolality through the base and feed additions, and culture duration by the day of harvest. The ranges carried into the control strategy are those of @sec-par-table.
2. A combined alert in the control system, which fires when `{python} ALERT_TXT` at the same time, the side of each that lowers acidic variants. A PAR is one-dimensional, so the PAR edge of one parameter holds only while the parameters that act with it stay within limits, and here those limits lie inside their NORs. Each limit is the most unfavourable value of its parameter at which the lower 95 % limit of a single run still meets the criterion of `{python} pct(ACC['acidic_variants'][0])`, with the other factors of the model at their unfavourable NOR edges. The alert covers every combination inside the NOR that fails the criterion. Osmolality is not a factor of the response-surface design, so the harvest action limit of item 3 covers it. The NOR is read as the range that the batch record controls, about ±3 standard deviations of the chance variation of each parameter (PCMP-001 §6.4).
3. An action limit for acidic variants at harvest of `{python} pct(MIT['action_limit'], 2)`, the lower limit of the criterion plus `{python} f"{MIT['guard']:g}"` intermediate-precision standard deviations of icIEF (`{python} MIT['method']`, `{python} fx(MIT['sd'])` points). A result below it is found before purification, although it cannot change the batch.
4. Acidic variants at harvest of every production batch trended against the initial viable cell concentration of the batch, so that the univariate effect of @sec-univariate is confirmed or found to be a false positive.
5. The KPPs are held within their NORs for process consistency. The delivered feed is checked by the mass reconciliation after the run, which detected DEV-003-02. The basal medium is prepared at its set-point under SOP-2004.
6. The drug substance criteria of the attributes this step sets apply at release (PCMP-001 §3). The glycans, acidic variants and aggregate are tested there by the methods of @sec-analytical.
7. The host cell protein that this step releases into the harvest is cleared by Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange, and is judged at each of those steps and at the drug substance. Residual DNA is cleared by the same steps and judged at the drug substance only (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008).
8. Process performance qualification (PPQ) at the receiving site under PTP-001 runs the process at its set-points. It confirms the process at scale near the centre of the NOR and does not test the edges of the ranges.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The conclusions of this report rest on the scale-down model, whose offsets are known well enough that no verdict over the NOR depends on their exact size. Four facts limit how far that holds. The offset was estimated at the set-points only, so its use toward the edges of the range studied is an assumption. The carbon dioxide stripping of the commercial vessel was not matched, and osmolality was set independently of pCO2 (@sec-operation). The growth and titre of the runs are not in the record, so the model cannot be compared with manufacturing scale on process performance (PD-003-09). The difference in aggregate between the scales has no known cause (PD-003-13).

The following limitations apply to the conclusions of this report.

1. For aggregate only `{python} AUG_IN_AGG` of the `{python} AUG_N` augmentation runs fall inside the 95 % prediction intervals of the model selected on the planned runs, so the single-run intervals of aggregate understate the scatter between runs (@sec-augmentation).
2. At the set-point the model of acidic variants predicts above the centre points and the manufacturing batches by more than the margin of its worst-corner median above the lower limit (@sec-models). For acidic variants, `{python} NEAR_OTHERS['acidic_variants']` other models have an AICc within `{python} f"{NEAR_D:g}"` units of the lowest, and only `{python} term_names(ACID_COMMON)` are common to all of them. Each gives acidic variants the same verdict over the NOR.
3. Osmolality has no PAR from a model, and its interactions with the other parameters are known only from the screening design (PD-003-07).
4. The effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants comes from a single significant result of a univariate study, which cannot show its interactions, and the multivariate study that PCP-003 §6.4 calls for has not been made (PD-003-11). The capability does not include it.
5. The pCO2 settings of the augmentation and osmolality studies rest on equipment whose calibration status is not recorded (PD-003-12).

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. The relationship of each parameter with each attribute was quantified (objective 1). The selected response-surface models describe the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` attributes over the ranges studied, and culture pH interacts with most of the other parameters.
2. The multivariate region was defined on the 95 % prediction interval of a single run (objective 2). It covers `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])` of the region studied, `{python} pct(100 * ALT_PLAN['ds'])` on the planned runs alone, and its boundary is set by the lower limit of acidic variants. The NOR does not lie entirely inside it (PD-003-08).
3. A PAR was established for each response-surface parameter and each attribute whose selected model has a significant term in it, `{python} N_SIGT` in all (objective 3). Every PAR contains the NOR on all runs, and on the planned runs alone three PARs for acidic variants do not. Osmolality has no PAR from a model.
4. Each parameter was classified (objective 4). The step has `{python} words(NCLS['WC-CPP'])` WC-CPPs, `{python} words(NCLS['CPP'])` CPP, `{python} words(NCLS['KPP'])` KPPs and `{python} words(NCLS['GPP'])` GPP.
5. The capability supports the control strategy of @sec-control (objective 5). The lowest Cpk of the drug substance is that of acidic variants, `{python} fx(ACAP.Cpk)`, between the minimum and the target of PCMP-001, and every other attribute that the step sets has a Cpk above the target.
6. The scale-down model is qualified for every output with a criterion.
7. Against the completion criteria of PCP-003 §7, the study is complete except that the design space does not contain the NOR for acidic variants (PD-003-08), osmolality has no PAR from a model (PD-003-07), and the multivariate study of the initial viable cell concentration was not made (PD-003-11).

# Study events and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-record}

PCP-003 calls a departure from the plan a deviation. A process characterization study is not GMP manufacture, so this report records the events of execution as study events, under the numbers Version 1.0 gave them, and every departure from the plan as a discrepancy from the plan. A discrepancy is work that the plan did not foresee, or a requirement of the plan that was not met, however late it was found. @tbl-dev-register lists the `{python} words(N_DEV)` study events of this step, and @tbl-disc-register the `{python} N_PD` discrepancies from PCP-003.

## DEV-003-01, pCO2 probe drift during screening run 4 {#sec-dev-01}

During screening run 4 the pCO2 probe of the scale-down system, EQ-BRX-205, read `{python} pv('co2', DRIFT)` higher than the offline reference, and the comparison of the two in in-process monitoring detected the drift. The controller held the probe reading at the design level of `{python} pv('co2', R4_CO2)`, so the run ran at about `{python} pv('co2', R4_REC)`. The record gives the cause as drift of the probe between two calibrations, and the equipment record shows the probe in calibration at the time of execution.

The run is analysed at its recorded setting, a shift of `{python} fx(abs(DRIFT_CODED), 3)` in coded units, in which 1 is the half-range of pCO2. With the run at its design setting instead, the set of significant effects is the same for every attribute. With run 4 excluded the screening model keeps `{python} words(R4['afucosylation']['excl_df'])` residual degrees of freedom. Fewer effects then reach significance for `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in R4_FEWER])`, and for afucosylation the same number, but not the same set. The run stayed in the analysis. The record names screening run 4 only. The response-surface design ran later on the same probe, and the record shows no recalibration between the two designs, so it does not show whether the probe read high in those runs too.

## DEV-003-02, nutrient feed-1 under-delivery on a centre-point batch {#sec-dev-02}

A centre-point batch of the screening design received `{python} pct(float(dev_003_02_feed_deficit_pct))` less nutrient feed-1 than its target, from lot LOT-FED-3120. The mass reconciliation after the run detected it, and its cause was a calibration offset of the feed pump. The batch received a feed volume of about `{python} pv('feed_vol', FEED_DELIV, 1)`, inside the NOR of `{python} nor_txt('feed_vol')` and the range studied of `{python} range_txt('feed_vol')`, and the univariate study detected no effect of the nutrient feed-1 volume on any attribute across that range (@sec-univariate). The record shows `{python} words(int(dev_003_02_ver_n))` determinations of the glycans of the batch by the glycan map (SOP-3010, validated under AMV-3010). Their mean has a 95 % confidence interval of ± `{python} pct(float(dev_003_02_ci_hw), 2)` of the result. The record names the batch as a screening centre point but not its run number, and @tbl-centre gives the spread of the `{python} words(NC_SCR)` centre points. The run stayed in the analysis.

## PD-003-01, osmolality study {#sec-pd-01}

The osmolality study (@sec-osm-design) found a significant fall of afucosylation with osmolality, and no significant effect on acidic variants at the least favourable NOR combination of the other parameters (@sec-osmolality). Its fitted mean of acidic variants at the NOR high lies below the lower limit, and the acceptance of @sec-criteria-results covers that setting.

## PD-003-02, augmentation of the response-surface design {#sec-pd-02}

The `{python} N_AUG` runs added under INV-002 changed the selected models of `{python} words(len(AUG_CHANGED))` attributes, and the models selected on the planned runs predict them poorly for high mannose and aggregate. The PARs and the design space on the planned runs alone are given in @sec-augmentation. The full quadratic model of high mannose still exceeds the limit on overfitting on all runs.

## PD-003-03, model selection {#sec-pd-03}

With the plan's full quadratic model in place of the selected models, on all `{python} N_ALL` runs, high mannose would have no adequate model, and the PAR of pCO2 for acidic variants would not contain the NOR (@sec-augmentation). The selection also changes the criteria of this step through the verification of the downstream steps (@sec-criteria).

## PD-003-04, models that do not meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs {#sec-pd-04}

The selected models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RI_FAIL])` were used although their absolute residuals rise with the predicted value. No run of any model has a Cook's distance above the F median. With the standard deviation of the half of the predicted values in which each prediction lies, both attributes keep their verdict over the NOR (@sec-residuals).

## PD-003-05, duplicate univariate runs {#sec-pd-05}

The duplicate runs give the pooled standard deviation of the study, with `{python} UV_DF` degrees of freedom, against which each univariate difference was tested, including the effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants (@sec-univariate).

## PD-003-06, setting of osmolality {#sec-pd-06}

Because osmolality was set independently of pCO2, the screening design and the osmolality study estimate the two effects separately, and the PAR of pCO2 does not include the rise of osmolality that comes with pCO2 at scale (@sec-par-table).

## PD-003-07, osmolality not carried into the response-surface design {#sec-pd-07}

The screening showed osmolality active on acidic variants and on galactosylation (@sec-screening), and the Version 2.0 re-analysis of the screening results found that it had not been carried forward. Every prediction and PAR and the design space of this report are therefore conditioned on osmolality at its set-point. The osmolality study measured its effect at one combination of the other parameters (PD-003-01), and its interactions with them are known from the screening design only.

## PD-003-08, NOR not narrowed for acidic variants {#sec-pd-08}

Acidic variants do not meet their criterion over the NOR on the prediction interval of a single run (@sec-criteria-results), and the NOR was not narrowed as PCP-003 §7 requires. The Version 2.0 re-analysis against the criteria of PCMP-001 Version 2.0 found the departure. The risk was accepted as the producer's, on the grounds that @sec-criteria-results gives. A combined alert in the control system covers every failing combination inside the NOR. It fires when `{python} ALERT_TXT` at the same time. The action limit for acidic variants at harvest of `{python} pct(MIT['action_limit'], 2)` and the trending of @sec-control complete the mitigation.

## PD-003-09, viable cell density, viability and titre not in the record {#sec-pd-09}

PCP-003 §5.4 requires the culture to be monitored for viable cell density and viability, and §5.1 lists both, with the titre, among the outputs of the qualification. The monitoring records cannot be recovered. No criterion of this report depends on these outputs. Their absence means that the classes of the KPPs rest on platform knowledge for process performance (@sec-classification), and that the scale-down model was not compared with manufacturing scale on growth and titre.

## PD-003-10, univariate study started before the response-surface study {#sec-pd-10}

The univariate study started on `{python} S0('S-BRX-UNI')`, before the response-surface study started on `{python} S0('S-BRX-RSM')`, and the review of the execution dates under INV-001 found it. The sequence of PCP-003 §11 exists so that the factors of the response-surface design are chosen from the screening result. The screening study had ended on `{python} S1('S-BRX-SCR')`, before either study started, and the univariate parameters were assigned by RA-001 and were not candidates for the response-surface design. The order of the two studies therefore affects no analysis.

## PD-003-11, initial viable cell concentration not carried into a multivariate study {#sec-pd-11}

The univariate study showed acidic variants `{python} fx(UIV_D_MFG)` points higher at the high end of the initial viable cell concentration than at the low end, at manufacturing scale (@sec-univariate). The mechanism of PCP-003 §4.3 does not account for the effect, so PCP-003 §6.4 carries the parameter into a multivariate study and amends the plan. That was not done, because the univariate results were not analysed in Version 1.0. The Version 2.0 re-analysis of the univariate results found the departure. With the parameter at its NOR low and the other parameters at their least favourable NOR combination, the effect would take the predicted median of acidic variants to about `{python} pct(WCA_IV_MED, 2)`, below the lower limit. The effect is the only significant result among `{python} N_UV_TESTS` univariate tests and may be a false positive. The risk acceptance of PD-003-08 is extended to that combination, and acidic variants at harvest are to be trended against the initial viable cell concentration of each production batch (@sec-control). The verdict over the NOR and the capability of this report do not include the effect.

## PD-003-12, equipment and calibration status not recorded for the osmolality and augmentation studies {#sec-pd-12}

The records of the osmolality study S-BRX-OSM and of the augmentation S-BRX-AUG name no equipment and state no calibration status of the pCO2 probe, which PCP-003 §9 and preventive action PA3 of INV-001 require. The review of the study record found the gap, and the records cannot be completed. If the studies used EQ-BRX-205, its next calibration was due on `{python} PROBE_DUE`, before both studies started. pCO2 varied from `{python} pv('co2', PRM['co2'].prange[0])` to `{python} pv('co2', PRM['co2'].prange[1])` in the `{python} N_AUG` augmentation runs and was held at `{python} pv('co2', WCA['settings']['co2'])` in the osmolality study, so the accuracy of those settings is not documented. A probe that read high, as in study event DEV-003-01, would put the true pCO2 below the recorded level. Every selected model is fitted to the augmentation runs.

## PD-003-13, aggregate offset of the scale-down model accounted for, not investigated {#sec-pd-13}

PCP-003 Version 1.0 qualified the scale-down model for an output only where the two scales showed no statistically significant difference at p < 0.05, and it required the source of any difference to be investigated before the characterization runs. For aggregate the two scales differ under that test (p `{python} pfmt(V1T['aggregates_hmw'])`), and no investigation was made before the screening study started. The re-analysis of the qualification against the Version 1.0 test found it. Under PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.1 a scale-down model may differ in mean from manufacturing scale where its offset is known precisely enough, so the Version 1.0 test was stricter than the use of the model needs. Aggregate is judged through its offset, a ratio of `{python} fx(SDM['aggregates_hmw']['offset'], 3)` with a `{python} OFF_CI` % confidence interval of `{python} fx(SDM['aggregates_hmw']['lo'], 3)` to `{python} fx(SDM['aggregates_hmw']['hi'], 3)`, and the model is qualified for it (@tbl-sdm-offsets). The cause of the difference is not known.

# Appendix C. Full effect and coefficient tables {.unnumbered #sec-app-c}

@tbl-scr-afucosylation to @tbl-scr-aggregates give every effect of the screening models, in the factor codes of @tbl-factors. @tbl-coef-afucosylation to @tbl-anova-aggregates give the coefficients and the analysis of variance of the selected response-surface models of the attributes other than acidic variants, whose tables are in @sec-effects.

```{python}
#| output: asis
def scr_table(r):
    _d = SCRE[r].copy()
    for _c in ("Effect", "Coef.", "Std. err.", "t"):
        _d[_c] = _d[_c].map(lambda v: f"{v:.4f}".replace("-", "−"))
    _d["p-value"] = _d["p-value"].map(p3)
    return _d


for _r, _lab in zip(RESPS, ["afucosylation", "galactosylation", "high-mannose", "acidic-variants", "aggregates"]):
    print(md(scr_table(_r)))
    print()
    print(f": Effects of the screening model of {OUT[_r]}, as measured in the scale-down model. {{#tbl-scr-{_lab}}}")
    print()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
for _r, _lab in zip([r for r in RESPS if r != "acidic_variants"], ["afucosylation", "galactosylation", "high-mannose", "aggregates"]):
    _sc = "log" if _r in LOGR else "raw"
    print(md(coef_table(_r)))
    print()
    print(f": Coefficients of the selected model of {OUT[_r]}, on the {_sc} scale and in coded units. {{#tbl-coef-{_lab}}}")
    print()
    print(md(anova_table(_r)))
    print()
    print(f": Analysis of variance of the selected model of {OUT[_r]}, on the {_sc} scale. {{#tbl-anova-{_lab}}}")
    print()
```

# Appendix D. Analytical methods summary {.unnumbered #sec-app-d}

@tbl-methods gives the analytical methods of the studies with their precision and limit of quantitation, as the method records hold them.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_dm = csv("dev_methods.csv").set_index("id")
_amv = dict(AMV_REFS)
_sec = CFG.raw()["analytics"]["methods"]["sec"]
_spec = [("AMV-3010", "SOP-3010", "Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose", "harvest"),
         ("AMV-3011", "SOP-3011", "Aggregate (HMW)", "harvest"),
         ("AMV-3013", "SOP-3013", "Acidic variants", "harvest"),
         ("AMV-3012", "SOP-3012", "Host cell protein", "clarified harvest"),
         ("AMV-3014", "SOP-3014", "Residual DNA", "clarified harvest")]
_rows = []
for _a, _s, _attr, _smp in _spec:
    if _a in _dm.index:
        _pr = f"{float(_dm.loc[_a, 'precision_pct']):g} % (relative)"
        _lq = f"{float(_dm.loc[_a, 'loq']):g} {_dm.loc[_a, 'loq_unit']}"
    elif _a == _sec["id"]:
        _pr = f"{float(_sec['sd_abs']):g} points (absolute SD)"
        _lq = "not in the record"
    else:
        _pr = _lq = "not in the record"
    _rows.append([_amv[_a], _s, _a, _attr, _smp, _pr, _lq])
_md = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Method", "Procedure", "Validation", "Attributes", "Sample", "Precision", "LOQ"])
T.frame(_md, "Analytical methods of the production bioreactor studies, with their precision and limit of "
        "quantitation.", "tbl-methods",
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "l", "l", "P{3.2cm}", "P{1.9cm}", "P{2.4cm}", "P{1.8cm}"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Precision as the relative standard deviation of repeat results, or for SEC as an absolute standard "
                    "deviation in percentage points of HMW. LOQ, limit of quantitation.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```
